name: Joy Division
hook: Formed after watching the Sex Pistols play Manchester, and became the coldest, bleakest sound to come out of punk's aftermath.
blurb: Bernard Sumner and Peter Hook formed Joy Division in Salford after seeing the Sex Pistols play, with singer Ian Curtis and drummer Stephen Morris completing the band, one of the most directly documented lines from London punk's first spark to a completely different regional sound. Signed to Tony Wilson's Factory Records, their music was slower and starker than punk: Manchester's bleakness after its industry had gone, producer Martin Hannett's spacious, echo-heavy production, and Curtis's inward lyrics. Curtis had been diagnosed with epilepsy and depression, and he died by suicide in 1980, just before their planned first American tour. The other members formed New Order after his death.

signatureTracks.title: Love Will Tear Us Apart
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Released after Curtis's death, and the song that carried Joy Division's cold, melodic bleakness to a much wider audience.

signatureTracks.title: Transmission
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Built almost entirely from Peter Hook's melodic, high-register bassline carrying the song, a Joy Division signature.
